yearT1.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/18] Participants were a stratified random sample of all migrants granted an offshore visa to Australia between September 1993 and August 1995

country.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/18] The Longitudinal Survey of Immigrants to Australia (LSIA) data published by the Department of Immigration and Multicultural and Indigenous Affairs were analyzed.

sample_type.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/18] Participants were a stratified random sample of all migrants granted an offshore visa to Australia

ethnicity.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/18] We analyzed data of 1360 respondents from 17 countries/regions: United Kingdom, Italy, Germany, 'Other Western Europe' (mostly from Austria, France, and the Netherlands), Northern Europe (Denmark, Finland, Norway, and Sweden), Poland, Russia, Turkey, Singapore, China, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, India, U.S.A., Argentina, South Africa.

lag.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/18] Interviews were conducted three times: 4–5 months after arrival (T1), 16–17 months after arrival (T2), and approximately 3½ years after arrival (T3).
lag.warning: The intervals are 1 year (T2-T1) and 2.125 years (T3-T2), so there is no single typical lag.
